answers.answer: Shuffle all 4 Conflict III cards and put them face down at the bottom; shuffle all 9 II cards and deal 5 face down above them; shuffle all 3 I cards and deal 1 face down on top. Return unused I and II cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘face-down 10-card Conflict Deck’; return unused cards ‘without looking at them.’

answers.answer: In four-player play, a human starts at 1 VP; in three-player play, at 0 VP. In either game the human starts with two Agents on the Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board, 12 troops total (3 in the garrison and 9 in supply), and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup: score marker on 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0; two Agents on Leader; 3 troops in garrison, 9 in supply; take 1 water.

answers.answer: Yes, you may take a Reveal turn while Agents remain, but after Revealing your turns are skipped for the rest of that phase, so you cannot later take an Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from the Reveal boxes of cards revealed from the remaining hand, not cards played on Agent turns. At Clean Up, all cards in front of you from both kinds of turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: ‘Agent turns are optional’; ‘Once you've taken a Reveal turn, your turns are skipped’; Reveal turn resolves just-revealed cards then moves all cards to discard.

answers.answer: An Agent-turn card or destination effect cannot pay that same visit's entry cost: entry must be paid immediately before resolving either. You choose only one Agent icon, so one card sends one Agent. A card with no Agent icons cannot be used on an Agent turn; it can be revealed on a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay costs ‘before resolving any effects’; ‘one card can't send multiple Agents’; no-icon cards only on Reveal turns.

answers.answer: At a Combat space, deploy all three troops recruited that turn plus up to two of the four already in the garrison, for at most five troops. At a non-Combat space you do not deploy troops. Recruit troops from your personal supply into your garrison first; if the supply is empty, you cannot recruit more until troops return there.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: deploy ‘any or all units recruited during your current turn ... plus up to two more’; troop recruitment takes one from supply to garrison.

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon on a played card lets you send an Agent to any space connected to a post where you have a Spy, without recalling that Spy. Infiltrate recalls your Spy from a connected post to bypass another player's Agent at the destination (not your own Agent). Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy after you place an Agent to draw a card, and you must choose it immediately after placement, before space or card effects. The same Spy cannot pay for both Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence, though two different Spies can be used for those separate effects.
answers.evidence: Spies: Spy Agent icon ‘do not recall’; Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence definitions; same Spy cannot be recalled for both.

answers.answer: Strength is 11: two troops are 4, one sandworm is 3, and four revealed swords are 4. If your last unit is removed, your strength becomes 0 even if you revealed swords. You cannot play Combat Intrigue without at least one unit in the Conflict.
answers.evidence: Strength: troop = 2, sandworm = 3, sword = 1; ‘must have at least one unit’; Combat Intrigue requires a unit in Conflict.

answers.answer: Yes. A pass does not prevent you acting again after another player plays; the window closes only after all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to each player's supply (not garrison), sandworms return to the bank, and Combat markers reset to 0.
answers.evidence: Combat: ‘not required to pass just because you passed earlier’; ‘pass consecutively’; cleanup returns troops to supply and sandworms to bank.

answers.answer: In a four-player tie for first, each tied player gets the second reward; if exactly two tie, the other players compete for the third reward, but nobody wins the Conflict or takes its card. In a three-player tie for first, each gets the second reward and no other reward is given; nobody takes the card. A player with 0 strength receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: exactly two tied first in four players leave remaining players competing for third; three or fewer get no other reward; no winner takes card. Zero strength receives no reward.

answers.answer: Having one or more sandworms doubles your rewards once; additional sandworms do not multiply again, so two worms do not quadruple rewards. Control of a location and battle icons on a Conflict card cannot be doubled. For an optional reward of 1 VP for 3 spice, you may pay 3 spice for the doubled 2 VP reward, or pay 6 spice to gain 2 VP; the cost may be paid a second time to take the reward twice.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: ‘one or more’; control and battle icons cannot double; example permits paying 3 spice for 1 VP or 6 for 2.

answers.answer: After winning a Conflict, take its card face up into your supply, then check for a matching icon. The other matching card can be a face-up Conflict or Objective card in your supply; the matching pair must be flipped face down for 1 VP. During Endgame, a wild icon can match any one of the three icon types in your supply, also flipping the pair for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Combat winner procedure checks after taking the card; Battle Icons: ‘must’ flip matching pair; Endgame wild icon may match any one type.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; it is lost when falling below 2 and gained again on reaching 2. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained after falling below 4 and earned again on returning to 4; the first to 4 also gets the Alliance token and 1 VP, which is lost if the token is lost. Tying the current Alliance holder does not take the token; a challenger must rise above the holder (or the FAQ's separate holder-loses-Influence rule can transfer it).
answers.evidence: Victory Points: 2-Influence VP reverses below 2; 4-track bonus is retained; Alliance VP is tied to holding it; tying does not steal.

answers.answer: You may spend Persuasion before, between, or after Reveal effects during your Reveal turn. You may pool Persuasion from multiple sources to buy one card and split a source across multiple cards. The Imperium Row refills to five after a purchase, and you may buy a replacement immediately if you can afford it. Acquired cards go face up into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: Persuasion may be used ‘before, between, or after’; may pool or split; Row always five; acquired card face up in discard.

answers.answer: At each Maker space without an Agent, add 1 spice to its bonus spot during Makers; visiting a Maker space gains all bonus spice there. Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or, with Hooks, two worms; Hagga Basin costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one worm. Worm choices still gain all bonus spice. Hooks are retained, not spent. A worm cannot go in a garrison and cannot be summoned to Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin while the Shield Wall remains; once Wall is removed, it can be summoned to any Conflict.
answers.evidence: Makers and Board Space Guide; Sandworms: Hooks not spent, never in garrison; Shield Wall protects the three named Conflicts.

answers.answer: The Endgame is triggered at Recall, at the end of a round, if anyone has 10+ VP or the Conflict Deck is empty. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigue cards, then compare VP. The rulebook resource tiebreakers are spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Scoring: ‘At the end of a round’; first play Endgame Intrigue, then most VP; ties use spice, Solari, water, garrison troops.

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM setup exposes 2 face-up contracts and puts the remaining standard contracts face down in the bank: 18 if Shaddam is not chosen, 16 if he is chosen because two Sardaukar contracts are set aside. Shuffle in 4 additional Intrigue and 4 additional Imperium cards. Shaddam is optional. The 10 contrasting-back Rise of Ix contracts are excluded from standard CHOAM and remain in the box.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup changes: two face-up offers; 20 standard contracts or 18 plus two reserved; add 4 cards to each deck; contrasting-back contracts only Rise of Ix.

answers.answer: With CHOAM, a contract icon takes one of the two face-up contracts into your supply and replaces it with a face-up token from the bank; if all contracts have been taken, the icon instead gives 2 Solari. A Harvest contract completes by visiting a Maker space and gaining the listed amount of spice that turn in total, including other sources. Immediate completes as soon as taken. Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: Taking contracts: take a face-up token and replace; if none remain icon gives 2 Solari. Completing contracts defines Harvest, Immediate, Acquire.

answers.answer: No. If you take a board-space contract after already sending your Agent to its named space that turn, you must wait until a future turn; you must have held it when sending the Agent. On completion, announce it, gain its shown rewards, and flip it face down while leaving it in your supply.
answers.evidence: Completing contracts: already-sent Agent requires a future turn; on completion announce, gain rewards, flip face down and leave in supply.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival as the third competitor. The Rival gets the Ornithopter Objective; the humans get the other two eligible Objectives, and the human with the First Player-marked card is First Player. First Player alternates only between the two humans. Turn order begins First Player, then Rival, then the other human; the Rival never takes a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: ‘one shared scoring Rival’; Rival gets Ornithopter; order First Player → Rival → other human; ‘Rival never Reveals.’

answers.answer: For an occupied indicated destination, the Rival ignores it and reveals another Hagal card. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: it tries an empty post of its specified type, ignores placement if none is open, and in either case immediately reveals another card. Ignore normal space costs and effects; use only Hagal effects. If the House Hagal deck empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle it and continue.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: ignore occupied destination and reveal again; Place Spy continues turn; ignore normal costs/effects; reshuffle on empty or Reshuffle.

answers.answer: Shuffle the Objective cards after removing those whose 1–3P or 4/6P marking does not match the player count; distribute one random eligible card face up to each player. Whoever has the First Player marker on their Objective takes the marker. Shaddam may not be chosen without the CHOAM Module.
answers.evidence: Setup: omit mismatched Objectives, distribute one random face-up card; First Player marker determines first player; do not use Shaddam unless CHOAM.

answers.answer: Solari, spice, water and sandworms are not limited; make a convenient substitution if the bank runs out. Troops are limited by the personal supply: if it is empty, you cannot recruit more until troops return there. Gains come from the bank and payments are returned to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup: resources and sandworms ‘not meant to be limited’; troop recruitment stops if supply empty; resource payments return to bank.

answers.answer: The five phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal the top Conflict card, resolve any controlled-location defensive troop bonus, then each player draws five cards. If Recall does not trigger Endgame, humans return Agents to Leaders; with 3–4 humans pass First Player clockwise, while in two-player return Rival Agents to its supply and pass First Player to the other human.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure lists phases and Round Start reveal before drawing five; Recall describes Agent returns and First Player passage.

answers.answer: Yes. After paying entry costs and satisfying requirements, you may resolve board-space and played Agent-box effects in any order, and the Faction advance is included in those effects. You cannot use Influence from that visit to meet its own entry requirement, because requirements must be met and costs paid before resolving any space or card effects.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay costs and meet requirements before effects; space, Agent-box and Influence effects may be carried out in any order.

answers.answer: An optional arrow cost and its effect can be used only once per turn, so you cannot pay it repeatedly in one Agent turn; the stated exception is sandworm reward doubling on a Conflict reward. Most card and space effects are mandatory, with exceptions including ‘may,’ declinable arrow costs, and the optional black-X trash icon. Intrigue costs and conditions must be met to play it; you cannot play it without paying its costs.
answers.evidence: Arrows: pay/effect once per turn except doubled Conflict rewards; FAQ: most effects mandatory, optional exceptions and Intrigue costs must be met.

answers.answer: Place a Spy from your supply on an unoccupied observation post. If none are in supply when needed, you may first recall one of your Spies for no effect. If the placement effect specifies an Agent icon that must connect to the post, only a post connected to that specified icon is legal.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: place on unoccupied post; may first recall for no effect; some effects specify the connected Agent icon.

answers.answer: No, Infiltrate bypasses another player's Agent, not your own. Spy recall is a special option without a card, but it does not replace the card required to take an Agent turn. You cannot recall two Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on one placement; you may recall one for Gather Intelligence and another for Infiltrate when both apply.
answers.evidence: Spies: Infiltrate cannot bypass own Agent; FAQ says recall still requires playing a card for Agent turn; two different Spy effects allowed, never two Gather Intelligence.

answers.answer: The controller gets 1 Solari when any player visits Arrakeen or Spice Refinery, or 1 spice when anyone visits Imperial Basin; if the controller is also the visitor, they receive both the visitor effect and controller bonus. Winning the matching Conflict places your Control marker there, replacing an opponent's. When a Conflict for a location you already control is revealed, you may deploy one troop from your supply directly to the Conflict without an Agent visit.
answers.evidence: Critical Locations & Control: winning sets/replaces control; controller bonus on any visit; defensive troop when Conflict revealed.

answers.answer: When two tie for second, each gets the third reward; the first-place winner keeps the first reward and Conflict card, with no further rewards. Players tied for third receive nothing. If three tie for first, each gets the second reward; nobody else gets a reward and nobody takes the Conflict card.
answers.evidence: Combat ties table: second ties receive third reward and winner keeps card; third ties get nothing; three tied first get second only and no card.

answers.answer: In a three-player Conflict with three different positive strengths, first and second place receive their normal rewards and third place receives nothing. This remains true when one of the participants is the Rival in a two-human game; it counts as a three-player game, so the Rival competes for the ordinary first and second rewards and third has no reward absent a second-place tie.
answers.evidence: Combat: with 2 or 3 players, ordinary first and second get rewards; ordinary third gets nothing; two humans plus Rival count as 3.

answers.answer: Plot Intrigues may be played during your own Agent or Reveal turn; Combat Intrigues only during Combat and only if you have a unit in the Conflict; Endgame Intrigues only at the end of the game. Keep Intrigues face down, separate from your deck, and reveal only when played; resolved cards go face up in a discard pile beside the Intrigue Deck. If the Intrigue deck runs out, shuffle its discard into a new deck.
answers.evidence: Intrigue cards: timing by type, keep face down separate, resolved cards discarded face up; FAQ covers reshuffling exhausted deck.

answers.answer: An ordinary discard instruction cannot discard an Intrigue unless it specifically says so. It discards a card of your choice from your hand, not a card in play or in your discard pile. The Secrets steal effect takes one Intrigue at random from each opponent who has four or more Intrigue cards.
answers.evidence: Discarding: from hand, not Intrigue unless specified; Secrets/Steal Intrigue: each opponent with 4+ gives one selected at random.

answers.answer: A trash effect can remove cards from your hand, discard pile or in play; return ordinary trashed cards to the box and Reserve cards to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless paying a cost or a card instructs you to trash itself. The VP gained from The Spice Must Flow's acquire effect is retained even if the card is later trashed.
answers.evidence: Trashing: lists eligible locations and destinations; optional exceptions. FAQ Victory: The Spice Must Flow acquire VP retained if trashed.

answers.answer: An acquire-box effect resolves once, at the moment the card is acquired. When you cannot draw because your deck is empty, reshuffle your discard pile into a new deck and continue drawing. Unused Persuasion cannot be saved; it is lost at the end of your Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Acquire box: effect at acquisition; Acquiring Cards: reshuffle discard when deck empty and unused Persuasion lost.

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and cards revealed on your Reveal turn are in play until Clean Up, unless trashed first. Fremen Bond can use one or more other Fremen cards in play; two Bond cards can activate each other regardless of play order. They cease being in play when Clean Up moves them to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond: cards remain face up through Clean Up; two Bond cards activate one another regardless of order.

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the Agent just placed this turn; the returned Agent may be used again on another Agent turn in the same round. Retreat moves a troop from Conflict to your garrison. ‘Retreat any number’ can mean zero.
answers.evidence: Recall Agent icon; Retreat and FAQ Combat and troops entries.

answers.answer: A free-choice effect granting two Influence must put both advances with one Faction; it cannot be split between Factions. A Faction-specific minimum-Influence effect requires meeting that stated threshold, and an Alliance-icon effect requires holding that Faction's Alliance token.
answers.evidence: Influence: free-choice gain two chooses any one Faction, not two; minimum and Alliance icon requirements stated.

answers.answer: If the holder loses Influence after being tied with two opponents, the formerly tied opponents are eligible and the former holder chooses which one receives the Alliance. If the holder falls to 3 or lower and no one has 4+, return the token to the board; the former holder loses its 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Victory Points / FAQ Alliance loss: if several tied, former holder chooses recipient; if holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4+, return token.

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is immediately revealed and used that turn. A card drawn after Reveal stays for the next round, then draw the usual five additional cards for that round. A Plot Intrigue played earlier whose effect applies at Reveal stays face up until then, is used, and then discarded.
answers.evidence: FAQ Draw timing states all three timing outcomes.

answers.answer: No. A ‘when you win a Conflict’ Intrigue cannot be played after tying for first because nobody wins. If you receive such an Intrigue as a reward for an outright win, it can be played immediately.
answers.evidence: FAQ Combat and troops: cannot play after tie; if received as winning reward can be played immediately.

answers.answer: If final VP and all listed resource tiebreakers remain tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed 12.
answers.evidence: FAQ Victory: if all four resource tiebreakers tied, most recent Reveal wins; scores may exceed printed track's 12.

answers.answer: No. You must complete all contracts you hold for that space with one Agent placement, and you must have held each when sending the Agent; you cannot delay them for a later visit after qualifying. Contract completion is another effect of that Agent turn and may resolve in any order with board-space and Agent-box effects.
answers.evidence: FAQ Contract completion is mandatory: fulfill all same-space contracts with one placement; completion is another effect resolved in any order.

answers.answer: No, Shaddam does not begin with the set-aside Sardaukar contracts. During setup set both aside before the initial contract shuffle; when he acquires a contract, he may choose one instead of a public one, and no other player may acquire them. This leaves 18 contracts to shuffle for two face-up offers and 16 in the bank. His Signet Ring deployment restriction starts immediately when he plays Signet Ring to send an Agent and lasts for that turn only, not the whole round.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup and Reserved Sardaukar contracts; FAQ Shaddam clarifies immediate restriction lasts for turn, not round.

answers.answer: Feyd starts with the token on the leftmost Training-track space; at the rightmost space it stays there for the rest of the game. Lady Jessica begins with the Lady Jessica side face up, not Reverend Mother Jessica; Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: Feyd token setup/rightmost; Lady Jessica setup side; FAQ says Reverend Mother Jessica may act on flip turn.

answers.answer: Yes, moving from 1 to 3 Influence counts as reaching 2 even when passing it while gaining multiple Influence. Margot/Irulan can reach 2 with the same Faction again after losing Influence and later regaining it; moving down through 2 does not count. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild's Favor from in play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding it from your hand does.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: passing 2 counts; can reach again by losing/regaining, only moving up; Guild's Favor Clean Up clarification.

answers.answer: Accept Contract uses Spice Trade access, has no cost, is not a Combat space, always draws one card, and resolves the contract icon: without CHOAM or when all contracts are taken it gives 2 Solari; with available CHOAM contracts it takes a contract. It gives no automatic Influence. Dutiful Service uses Emperor access, has no cost, is not a Combat space, gains 1 Emperor Influence and resolves the same contract-icon alternatives; it automatically advances Emperor Influence once, not twice.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table and Faction status: Accept Contract is non-Faction; Dutiful Service is Emperor and Influence counted once.

answers.answer: Arrakeen: City access, no cost, Combat space; visitor recruits one troop and draws one card, while its controller gains 1 Solari. Fremkit: Fremen access, no cost, Combat space; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw one card. Research Station: City access, costs 2 water, Combat space; recruit two troops and draw two cards.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide entries for Arrakeen, Fremkit and Research Station.

answers.answer: Deep Desert costs 3 water, offers 4 base spice or, if you have Maker Hooks, two sandworms. Hagga Basin costs 1 water, offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one sandworm. At either space, also gain all accumulated bonus spice regardless of choosing worms. Hooks are not spent when summoning.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Deep Desert/Hagga Basin; Maker and sandworm rules say gain all bonus spice and Hooks retained.

answers.answer: Both options require City access and 2+ Fremen Influence, with no resource entry cost. Option one: take a Maker Hooks token if you lack one, recruit one troop, and gain 1 water. Option two: gain 1 water and optionally remove the Shield Wall; it does not recruit a troop.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Sietch Tabr entry and options.

answers.answer: High Council is Landsraad access, not a Combat space. First visit costs 5 Solari and places your Councilor on an unoccupied seat; thereafter gain 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. Later visits still cost 5 Solari and instead give 2 spice, draw an Intrigue, and recruit three troops.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide High Council row.

answers.answer: Swordmaster costs 8 Solari before anyone gains a Swordmaster and 6 Solari once anyone has one. Each player may gain it only once per game. The third Agent is available this round and for the rest of the game. A Rival obtaining its Swordmaster also reduces the human cost to 6.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Swordmaster row: once per player; Rival gaining one reduces human cost.

answers.answer: Imperial Privilege is Landsraad access, non-Combat, requires 2+ Emperor Influence, and costs 3 Solari. Its effects let you discard an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue, and recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. It recalls another Agent, not the one just placed; it does not automatically grant Emperor Influence.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Imperial Privilege row; Influence rules only Faction spaces automatically advance track.

answers.answer: Shipping uses Spice Trade access, is non-Combat, requires 2+ Spacing Guild Influence, and costs 3 spice. It gains 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction; that free-choice Influence need not be Guild.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Shipping row.

answers.answer: Gather Support is a non-Combat Landsraad space: recruit two troops at no cost, or pay 2 Solari and also gain 1 water. Spice Refinery is a Combat City space: pay 0 spice to gain 2 Solari or pay 1 spice to gain 4 Solari; its controller also gains 1 Solari on the visit.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Gather Support and Spice Refinery rows.

answers.answer: Heighliner: Spacing Guild Combat space, costs 5 spice, gains 1 Guild Influence and recruits five troops. Desert Tactics: Fremen Combat space, costs 1 water, gains 1 Fremen Influence, recruits one troop, and optionally trashes a card. Sardaukar: Emperor non-Combat space, costs 4 spice, gains 1 Emperor Influence, draws an Intrigue, and recruits four troops. Normal deployment is allowed at Heighliner and Desert Tactics, not Sardaukar.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide entries for Heighliner, Desert Tactics and Sardaukar, including Combat column.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall is Landsraad access, non-Combat, no cost: draw an Intrigue and gain 1 Persuasion during your Reveal turn if your Agent is there. Espionage is Bene Gesserit access, non-Combat, costs 1 spice: gain 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draw a card and place a Spy. Deliver Supplies is Spacing Guild access, non-Combat, no cost: gain 1 Guild Influence and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows for Assembly Hall, Espionage and Deliver Supplies.

answers.answer: False Orders makes affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent's destination that turn; it may be played even if no enemy Spy is connected there. Litany Against Fear's red box is ignored during Reveal, or when it gains an Agent icon and is played as an Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ: False Orders and Litany Against Fear clarifications.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the card removed by Manipulate. You may acquire it by other means, but without its 1-Persuasion discount. If it has not been acquired by the end of your next Reveal turn, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: FAQ Manipulate: opponents cannot acquire; no discount by other means; remove at end of next Reveal.

answers.answer: The standard two-player Rival starts with four cubes at the bottom of the Influence tracks, three troops in its garrison and remaining troops in supply, two Agents in supply and Swordmaster beside the board, three Spies and 1 water in supply; score and Combat marker at 0. Shuffle House Hagal and keep the 2P Reshuffle card in the deck near the Rival. Its 10+ VP triggers Endgame at Recall, and the Rival can win by having the most VP.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules setup and scoring statement.

answers.answer: The Rival immediately spends resources and takes its third Agent as soon as its combined eligible total reaches the printed Swordmaster threshold; the Agent is usable that current round. Count Solari, spice, Intrigue cards and water, one each. Spend Solari first, then spice, Intrigue cards, then water, and keep any leftovers.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources and Swordmaster: threshold, count and priority sequence, leftovers and current-round use.

answers.answer: After it has Swordmaster, the Rival spends each exact set of 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water for 1 VP. It does not spend any mixed total of seven resources for a VP.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources: ‘whenever it has 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water, spend each such set for 1 VP.’

answers.answer: When choosing Influence, the Rival uses the Faction where it has least Influence, breaking ties by the leftmost priority icon on its Rival card. Like a human it gets the 2-Influence VP and Alliance VP; it does not receive the resource bonus for reaching 4. A numbered Hagal Influence icon means the corresponding position in the Rival's Faction priority list.
answers.evidence: Rival rules: gains/loses Influence VP and Alliances like human but no resource bonus at 4; numbered icon and least-Influence priority described.

answers.answer: No. With a two-destination Hagal card, choose only the destination matching current conditions; if that destination is occupied, reveal a new card without using the other destination. Guild Influence selects between Accept Contract and Shipping; Conflict tier selects between Deliver Supplies and Heighliner.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: choose only condition-matching destination; occupied means reveal a new card; lists both condition pairs.

answers.answer: Yes. At every Rival Combat space it deploys up to two available troops from its garrison even if the card recruited none. Newly recruited troops at a non-Combat space go to garrison. A conditional bonus at 2+ Influence that it does not meet does not prevent placing the Agent; it simply gets no bonus.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: deploy up to two at every Combat space even if no recruit; recruits elsewhere to garrison; missing 2+ bonus never prevents placement.

answers.answer: Unless a post type is specified, the Rival places a Spy at the first available Faction observation post in its priority order; if all four are occupied, ignore placement. Placing its third and final supply Spy immediately recalls its other two Spies and triggers its printed Scheme. Rivals never recall Spies to Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes rules.

answers.answer: Troops recruited by a Scheme before the Rival places an Agent at a Combat space that same turn can deploy there. If a Place Spy card has no legal empty post, ignore the placement, then immediately reveal another Hagal card because the card did not send an Agent.
answers.evidence: Rival rules: Scheme-recruited troops can deploy same turn; Place Spy continues turn whether or not a post is open.

answers.answer: At Hagga Basin or Deep Desert, the Rival always collects all accumulated bonus spice. With Hooks and a Conflict that permits summoning, it summons one worm at Hagga or two at Deep Desert instead of taking base spice. If it summons none—because it lacks Hooks or the Conflict is Shield Wall-protected—it takes base spice instead: 2 at Hagga, 4 at Deep Desert. The Shield Wall removal effect itself works only if it has Hooks and the Wall remains.
answers.evidence: Rival Maker spaces: bonus spice always collected; Hooks/worm choices and base spice; protected Conflicts and Wall effect conditions.

answers.answer: At the beginning of Combat, if the Rival has at least one unit deployed, reveal one Hagal card and add its bottom swords to strength; on Reshuffle, reshuffle and reveal again. This occurs before humans' normal Combat Intrigue window, so humans can act afterward. If the Rival has no deployed unit, it gets no bonus.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat: beginning of Combat, unit prerequisite, bottom swords, reshuffle behavior; humans then get window.

answers.answer: Yes. The Rival receives control bonuses on visits, gets the defensive troop from supply when its controlled location Conflict is revealed, gains battle-icon VP, and doubles Conflict rewards with worms. It always takes an optional Conflict VP if able to pay or recall the required Spies. It never takes contracts; even with CHOAM, a contract reward gives it 2 Solari.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat: control/defensive bonuses, battle icon and doubled reward behavior; optional VP and no-contract rule.

answers.answer: During the Reveal effects step, total and announce strength and set the Combat marker at any point while resolving; update it as needed, so the total is not fixed for the entire turn. If strength exceeds 20, flip the marker to its +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn and Strength: set strength at any point while resolving; over 20 flip marker to +20 and restart track.

answers.answer: A Leader's Signet Ring ability activates when you play Signet Ring on one of your Agent turns, not merely when you reveal it. Card text can override the usual rules of the game.
answers.evidence: Setup: right Leader ability marked Signet Ring activates when playing Signet Ring on Agent turn; Overview: cards can override usual rules.

answers.answer: A Recall Spy icon on a card returns one of your Spies from a post to your supply, usually as a cost for a powerful effect. It is not automatically Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those are separate optional recalls without a card that produce their own specified effects.
answers.evidence: Spies: Recall Spy icon returns Spy to supply; Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence separately described as recalls without a card.

answers.answer: The trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. An ordinary discard instruction discards a card from your hand but cannot select an Intrigue unless it specifically allows it; it does not trash the card.
answers.evidence: Trashing: separate trash-an-Intrigue icon; Discarding: Intrigues excluded unless specified.

answers.answer: Yes, the doubled Conflict reward may be taken twice, and each choice of 1 Influence can be with the same or a different Faction. By contrast, a single effect granting two Influence with free choice requires both advances on one Faction.
answers.evidence: Sandworm reward example: 2 Influence may be same or two different Factions; Influence rules say a single gain-two choice cannot split.

answers.answer: Resolve the Signet Ring ability printed on the selected Rival card. The Scheme is not substituted. This trigger requires no human Signet Ring card or human Reveal turn; it is the Hagal Signet Ring icon that triggers the Rival ability.
answers.evidence: Rival Signet Ring and Scheme table: Hagal Signet icon resolves Rival's Signet Ring ability; no human Signet or Reveal involved.

answers.answer: A Maker Hooks icon gives one token from the bank if the Rival lacks Hooks; if it already has one, it gets no additional token. A Shield Wall removal icon removes the Wall only if it has Hooks and the Wall remains. Without Hooks, ignore it; if the Wall is already gone, it has no further effect.
answers.evidence: Rival Hooks and Wall icons table.

answers.answer: Secrets is Bene Gesserit access, has no entry cost, and is not a Combat space. It gains 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draws one Intrigue from the Intrigue Deck, and each opponent with at least four Intrigues gives one of their Intrigues selected at random.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Secrets row and Steal Intrigue rule.

answers.answer: Imperial Basin uses Spice Trade access, has no entry cost, and is a Combat space. The visitor gains 1 base spice plus all bonus spice there; its controller gains 1 spice. If the visitor is also the controller, that player gets both amounts, for 2 total plus bonus spice.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide Imperial Basin: ‘1 base spice plus all bonus spice; controller gains 1 spice.’

answers.answer: At Round Start, reveal the top Conflict and place it face up next to the deck, on top of any Conflict cards remaining from previous rounds; then resolve any controlled-location defensive troop bonus, and after that each player draws five cards.
answers.evidence: Round Start: reveal Conflict on top of previous cards, resolve defensive bonus, then draw five cards.

answers.answer: Each human places one cube on the bottom space of each of the four Faction Influence tracks. Place the four Alliance tokens on the marked areas of those tracks; nobody starts with an Alliance. The Shield Wall token is placed on the marked board area below Spice Refinery, so it is initially present.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 6: Alliance tokens on tracks; Shield Wall on board; cubes on bottom spaces.

answers.answer: In standard 3–4-player play, the player with the First Player marker takes the first turn and turns continue clockwise. A player who Reveals is skipped for the rest of Player Turns; that phase ends when all players have Revealed. In Combat Intrigue, First Player acts first and priority continues clockwise. An eligible player may play any number of Combat Intrigues or pass; passing does not bar a later play, and the window closes after all participants pass consecutively.
answers.evidence: Player Turns and Combat sections state order and end conditions; Combat Intrigue permits any number and consecutive passes.

answers.answer: The three steps are Reveal Cards (reveal all cards remaining in hand), Resolve Reveal Effects (resolve just-revealed cards' Reveal boxes and spend Persuasion), then Clean Up (move all cards in front of you to discard). Reveal effects may be resolved in any order, not card order.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn: three ordered steps; effects may be gained ‘in any order.’

answers.answer: Shuffle each human's 10-card starting deck and place it face down in their supply; without CHOAM omit CHOAM-marked cards before shuffling the Intrigue and Imperium decks, then place those decks face down. Deal five Imperium cards face up as the Row and set out Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow in separate Reserve stacks. The Combat marker begins at 0; the three Spies and Councilor are in the player's supply; Control markers are also in supply.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 4 and 6 and Initial card states table.

answers.answer: During a Reveal turn, you may ordinarily acquire one or more of the five face-up Imperium Row cards, Prepare the Way, or The Spice Must Flow. Each card's cost is at its top right. These ordinary Persuasion purchases happen during Reveal, not an Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: during Reveal use Persuasion on Row or Reserve; cost top right.

answers.answer: Yes. Ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional even when a legal post or Spy exists. The Shield Wall detonation/removal icon is an optional ‘may remove’ effect; once removed, the Wall returns to the box and cannot return in a later round.
answers.evidence: Spies: ordinary placement/recall optional; Shield Wall: may remove and is gone for rest of game.

answers.answer: Normally, a matching Agent icon on the played card must match the destination's access icon. A Spy merely connected to Shipping does not make a City-only card eligible for Shipping. If the card has the Spy Agent icon, that icon lets the Agent go to any space connected to a post where you have a Spy, without recalling it.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: matching icon required; Spy Agent icon specifically grants connected-space access; a connected Spy alone does not give access to every card.

answers.answer: Yes. On your Agent turn you may first play a legal Plot Intrigue; resources it grants before placement can be used to pay the destination cost. But resources gained after placement from the destination or the played Agent card cannot pay that same entry cost; those effects resolve only after the cost is paid.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Plot may be played before Agent placement and its prior gains pay; post-placement destination/card gains cannot pay entry.

answers.answer: No. In two-player play, even after both humans have Revealed, Player Turns continues while the Rival has Agents in supply; its remaining Agent turns are resolved. The Rival never takes a Reveal turn, and Combat begins only after both humans have Revealed and the Rival used all its Agents.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: in 2P continue Rival Agent turns after humans reveal; Combat only after both conditions; Rival never Reveals.

answers.answer: Standard 2–4-player spaces and access / Combat status: Accept Contract—Spice Trade, No; Arrakeen—City, Yes; Assembly Hall—Landsraad, No; Deep Desert—Spice Trade, Yes; Deliver Supplies—Spacing Guild, No; Desert Tactics—Fremen, Yes; Dutiful Service—Emperor, No; Espionage—Bene Gesserit, No; Fremkit—Fremen, Yes; Gather Support—Landsraad, No; Hagga Basin—Spice Trade, Yes; Heighliner—Spacing Guild, Yes; High Council—Landsraad, No; Imperial Basin—Spice Trade, Yes; Imperial Privilege—Landsraad, No; Research Station—City, Yes; Sardaukar—Emperor, No; Secrets—Bene Gesserit, No; Shipping—Spice Trade, No; Sietch Tabr—City, Yes; Spice Refinery—City, Yes; Swordmaster—Landsraad, No.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table lists 22 spaces with Agent access icon and explicit Combat? column.

answers.answer: When a Conflict for a location you already control is revealed at Round Start, its controller may deploy one troop from personal supply directly to the Conflict; this is optional and does not require an Agent visit. After Conflict rewards, all Combat markers reset to 0 before the next phase.
answers.evidence: Round Start defensive troop; Combat cleanup says markers reset to 0.

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up in front of you and send one Agent from your Leader to a legal unoccupied matching space. Resolve that card's Agent box, ignoring its Reveal box. You cannot reuse a card already in play or in discard as the card played, and cannot simply move an Agent already on the board; the summary specifies playing from hand and sending an Agent from your Leader.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: ‘Play one card from your hand’; Agent from Leader; resolve Agent box; discard/in-play handling described separately.

answers.answer: The restriction applies immediately when Shaddam plays Signet Ring to send an Agent, so he cannot deploy units first by choosing board-space effects before his Leader effect. It applies for that entire turn.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: restriction takes effect immediately; general freedom to order effects cannot postpone it.

answers.answer: With four different positive strengths and no sandworms, first, second and third place receive their printed rewards; fourth receives no reward. The highest-strength player wins and takes the Conflict card face up, then checks for a battle-icon match.
answers.evidence: Combat: with four players first, second and third can receive rewards; winner takes card; fourth not paid.

answers.answer: Players may choose Leaders or select them at random; random distribution is not required.
answers.evidence: Setup: each player takes a Leader ‘(choose, or select at random).’

answers.answer: An ordinary draw-a-card effect draws from your own deck, reshuffling your discard pile into a new deck if needed. You may not choose a card directly from your discard pile instead.
answers.evidence: Drawing cards: ordinary draw uses your own deck, not a chosen card from discard; reshuffle when empty.

answers.answer: Shuffle the House Hagal deck and place it near the shared Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card in the deck.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules setup: shuffle House Hagal and place near Rival, ‘retaining the 2P Reshuffle card.’

answers.answer: All four Maker Hooks tokens begin in the common bank; normal setup assigns none to a human. A token later acquired by a player moves from the bank onto that player's garrison.
answers.evidence: Setup: put all 4 Maker Hooks in common bank; acquired token moves onto player's garrison.

answers.answer: Yes. If a Combat Intrigue changes deployed units or otherwise changes strength, adjust the participant's Combat marker when that card resolves during the Combat Intrigue window. Use the adjusted strength shown on the track to determine Conflict rewards.
answers.evidence: Combat: marker must adjust when Combat Intrigue resolves; total set during Reveal is not fixed; resolve using adjusted track strength.

answers.answer: Gained Solari, spice and water come from the common bank, not another player's supply. When you pay these resources, return them to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup bank rule: gains take from bank; payments return to bank.

answers.answer: Shuffle the 20 standard contract tokens face down before revealing two face-up offers; put the rest face down in the bank. Players do not choose which two offers appear or preset the hidden order; the tokens are shuffled.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup: ‘Shuffle the remaining contract tokens face down, then flip two face up’; remaining face down in bank.

answers.answer: If Shaddam is chosen, set aside both Sardaukar contracts before shuffling; only Shaddam may acquire them, and setting them aside does not give them to him. Shuffle the remaining 18 standard contracts, expose two as public offers, and put 16 face down in the bank, with the two reserved contracts separate.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup and Reserved Sardaukar contracts specify set-aside timing, exclusivity, no starting possession, and 18/2/16 counts.
